title: March-May warmth had negative mean flight-date slopes in four England Meadow Brown samples in 1976-2024
abstract: We tested whether warmer springs were linked to earlier Meadow Brown flight dates in England. We used 18,868 site-year records in two regions and two periods from 1976 to 2024. Models controlled site effects and linear time. Mean flight-date slopes were -2.98, -2.09, -3.28 and -2.87 days per C. Three of four eight-test adjusted intervals were below zero. First observation date had a more negative slope than mean flight date in three samples. The early northern gap slope was uncertain. Peak-count controls, a high-count filter and a common-site check kept all four mean-date estimates negative. Site-trend and survey-season checks gave similar signs. These checks do not separate biological development from weather effects on adult activity and visits. Shared weather, selected sites, coarse temperature data and missing visit records limit inference. This test does not estimate an air pollution effect or a causal climate-change effect. The package gives model inputs, source hashes, code, uncertainty and an independent numerical check.

display.caption: Spring temperature slopes for mean flight date and first-minus-mean date. Bars give eight-test adjusted intervals. Site effects and linear time are controlled.

citations.reason: Prior butterfly abundance and heat study guided the distinct choice of site-level flight timing. The survey system overlaps.
